headline: Failed bill would have set deadlines for the FCC to decide on satellite license applications and added space safety and spectrum-sharing rules.
what_it_does: The bill would have required the Federal Communications Commission (FCC) to update its rules for licensing satellites and letting foreign satellites serve the U.S. market. The FCC would have had to decide on new applications or major changes within one year, renewals within 180 days, and minor changes within 90 days, with some extensions allowed, such as for national security concerns. The rules would also have had to include specific, measurable goals for space safety and orbital debris, plus requirements for satellite operators to coordinate and share radio spectrum without causing harmful interference.

who_it_affects.how: They would have gotten set deadlines for FCC decisions on their license applications, along with new space safety and spectrum-sharing requirements.

who_it_affects.group: Foreign satellite operators seeking to serve the U.S. market
who_it_affects.how: Their requests for U.S. market access would have been subject to the same decision deadlines and rules.

who_it_affects.group: Other authorized users of radio spectrum
who_it_affects.how: They would have received a defined, measurable level of protection from harmful interference by satellite operators.
The agency would have had to revise its satellite rules and meet deadlines for deciding on applications.
